mike: Heads up — canary for Dedicated rollout is blocked. Observed 2-3x increase in p99 latency on a subset of requests after merging PR #4123 (kernel selection heuristics). Rolling back canary now :warning:

sasha: ack. I saw CI perf jobs flake earlier today, looked related to batch-sizing changes in the same PR. CI job: https://ci.redwood/12345#perf-report shows regressed tail latency on long-context workloads.

kevin: Bisect points to commit abcdef1 (kernel selector tweak + batching heuristic). Reproducer on canary nodes: consistent 2.7x p99 on 8k context when KV cache hit rate > 70%.

jo: deploy-bot reports health-check slow responses during canary: 
```
[deploy-bot] health-check latency 1200ms (threshold 200ms) on node rwd-canary-02
model: redwood-v2-13b-quant
kernel: auto-selected cuBLAS_fused_v2
batch window: 25ms
KV cache hit: 78%
```

deploy-bot: Canary deployment paused by autoscaler. Perf regression alert created: PERF-2026-03-18-004.

lisa: Interesting that KV cache high-hit correlates. Could be a regression in how KV pages are compacted or cache eviction scheduling interacting with the new batching. Sasha, do you have flamegraphs?

sasha: Attached quick profiler snapshot from the canary node (sampled): CPU time spikes in kernel_selector::choose_kernel and in batch_scheduler::flush_path. Flame snippet: `choose_kernel` -> `compile_or_cache_kernels` -> `launch_attention_fused`. Also observed larger-than-usual memcpy spikes right before token emission.

ana: (note) customer success flagged one Dedicated customer reporting timeouts on steady load earlier this morning — potential SLA impact if rollout continues.

kevin: I started a local bisect: reverting the batching heuristics diff (PR #4130) locally brings p99 back to baseline. Kernel selection change alone has smaller effect. So likely interaction between kernel selection + new batching.

mike: Action items: 1) Hold rollout (done). 2) Open revert PR for batching heuristics (WIP by kevin). 3) Run targeted perf CI with KV cache stress matrix and long-context traces (sasha/ana). 4) Notify sales/CS and flag SLA risk.

kevin: Creating revert PR now: https://git.redwood/rw/runtime/pull/4172 — adding explicit revert of batching heuristics. Will run canary tomorrow after quick perf CI.

jo: Also adding temporary canary routing rule to avoid Dedicated customers in the affected pool. That should protect SLA while we investigate.

lisa: FYI we should include sampling for memcpy and kernel launch latencies in the perf dashboards so this doesn't slip. Filing a follow-up: PERF-DASH-417.

mike: Thanks all. If revert PR doesn't clear perf, next step is a full revert of both PRs and a hotfix to kernel selection fallback to previous strategy. Keep thread updated, will escalate to oncall if customers show repeat errors. :eyes:
